name: Ralph Brazelton Peck
summary: American civil engineer and geotechnical expert known for the observational method and soil mechanics.

name: Orwin K. Peck
summary: Civil engineer and father of Ralph Peck, worked in the railway sector.

name: Ethel Huyck Truby
summary: Mother of Ralph Peck and teacher.

name: Marjorie Elizabeth Truby
summary: Wife of Ralph Peck, graduated in chemistry.

name: Karl Terzaghi
summary: Austrian civil engineer and father of soil mechanics, mentor to Peck.

name: Arthur Casagrande
summary: Civil engineer who taught soil mechanics at Harvard University.

name: Albert Edward Cummings
summary: Geotechnical engineer and mentor to Peck at Raymond Concrete Pile Company.

name: Laurits Bjerrum
summary: Norwegian civil engineer and precursor of soil mechanics in Norway.

name: Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute
summary: Private technological research university in Troy, New York.

name: Harvard University
summary: University in Cambridge, Massachusetts, where Peck studied soil mechanics.

name: University of Illinois
summary: University where Peck was a professor for 32 years.

name: Winnipeg
summary: City in Manitoba, Canada, where Ralph Peck was born.

name: Albuquerque
summary: City in New Mexico, where Peck retired and died.

name: Chicago Subway Works
summary: Major infrastructure project where Peck worked as Terzaghi's representative.

name: Soil Mechanics in Engineering Practice
summary: Classic textbook on soil mechanics co-authored by Terzaghi and Peck.

name: Observational Method
summary: Constructive technique developed by Peck for geotechnical engineering.

name: Teton Dam
summary: Earth dam in Idaho that failed in 1976, investigated by Peck.

name: American Society of Civil Engineers
summary: Professional organization that awarded Peck multiple prizes.

name: Norwegian Geotechnical Institute
summary: Research institute where Peck collaborated with Bjerrum.
